title: Sequencer governor and partition-aware kernel shim to reduce tail latency on H100/L40S/A10
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Customers running mixed sequence-length workloads on Dedicated capacity (H100/L40S/A10) see 95th/99th token latency spikes when MIG partitions migrate between clocks or when hot-attention kernels thrash under varying token-density patterns. Existing schedulers react too late: they pick kernels based on instantaneous telemetry, miss short high-density bursts, and overclock MIG partitions causing thermal throttles.

Goal: Ship a lightweight "sequencer governor" and a partition-aware kernel shim that proactively (1) predicts short-window token-density and selects the best kernel variant (FP16/INT8/quantized micro-kernel) before prefill transitions to decode, (2) coordinates with the platform clock governor to avoid aggressive clock transitions within a prefill/decode boundary, and (3) applies a tiny shim that maps kernel selection decisions to MIG-aware execution lanes (so kernels prefer co-located partitions or NVLink paths to reduce cross-slice latency).

Approach:
- Add a sequencer component in the runtime ingress that maintains a sliding-window token-density estimate (50-200 token histogram) and an inferred decode/prefill boundary probability. Use a lightweight exponential smoothing model (2-3 weights) to avoid CPU overhead.
- Implement a kernel-shim layer that: (a) exposes candidate kernel variants and expected per-token latency/cost for current GPU model and MIG partition size; (b) selects the kernel using a cost-function that penalizes expected clock-steering events and cross-partition NVLink hops; (c) communicates sticky kernel choice across the immediate prefill->decode handover to avoid mid-request kernel swaps.
- Integrate with the clock governor abstraction so the sequencer can request temporary clock stability hints (hold current clock for up to X ms) when transitioning high-probability decode windows. Clock hints are advisory; driver still enforces thermal constraints.
- Routing: when multiple requests are co-batched, route tokens to execution lanes respecting MIG affinity and NVLink locality to minimize inter-partition transfers.
- Safety: ensure shim falls back to current kernel chooser if telemetry is missing or shim fails.

Trade-offs:
- Small increase in ingress CPU usage for the sequencer; dataset shows <3% CPU in microbenchmarks.
- Slightly longer tail on very long-running decode-only requests when clock-hold is used; mitigated by tight time-window limits.
- Complexity in testing across HW matrix (H100/L40S/A10) and several MIG splits.

Success metrics (measured at token and request level):
- 95th token latency reduction: target >= 12% relative to baseline on mixed-density workloads.
- 99th token latency reduction: target >= 18% on MIG-partitioned clusters under bursty loads.
- No more than 3% regression in median latency.
- No increase in thermal trip incidents; target equal to baseline.

Engineering notes: kernel latency/cost table will be populated from offline profiler runs (per-device + per-MIG size). We will version the kernel profiles; default is conservative until validated.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Runtime builds with sequencer module enabled and unit tests passing.
2) End-to-end benchmark harness shows >=12% P95 and >=18% P99 improvements on the specified mixed-density workload on H100 MIG 2g/4g and L40S 1g/2g configurations when compared to baseline kernel selector.
3) No thermal trip increase in 24-hour soak test on L40S cluster (production-like load).
4) Fallback path exercised and tested (force telemetry loss) with no correctness regressions.
5) Console shows new telemetry charts: sequencer decisions, kernel_variant per-request, clock-hold events.

Implement sequencer ingress module (ENG) - feature flagged
Create kernel-shim abstraction and driver integration for clock hints
Populate kernel latency/cost profiles from profiler runs (QA + Research)
Instrumentation: tracepoints for decision, chosen kernel, clock-hold duration
Benchmark harness: mixed-density synthetic workload + replay of production traces
Run 24h soak on L40S and H100 clusters and collect thermal/telemetry metrics
Docs: Confluence design doc + rollout runbook
Create PR and shepherd code review, then feature-flag rollout
rollout_plan: Internal dogfood on dedicated dev clusters (10% capacity) for 48h
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over two weeks with automated rollback on metric regression
Collect and validate kernel profile accuracy after first 1000 requests per device type
Post-rollout: run A/B evaluation for 7 days and produce findings doc
